results.name: Monjayaki on Monja Street
results.why_it_is_special: Tokyo's own savory pancake — runnier and more interactive than Osaka's okonomiyaki. Monja Street has 60+ shops where you cook it yourself on a tabletop griddle with small metal spatulas. This is the dish's birthplace and a deeply local tradition.

results.name: Tsukemen at Fuunji
results.why_it_is_special: Tsukemen (dipping ramen) is a Tokyo-born style where cold noodles are dipped into a concentrated broth. Fuunji is a pivotal shop in tsukemen history, famous for its rich fish-based broth, and still draws both locals and visitors.

results.name: Tonkatsu at Tonki
results.why_it_is_special: Operating since 1939, Tonki is one of Tokyo's most celebrated tonkatsu (deep-fried pork cutlet) institutions. The stadium-like open kitchen on the first floor is part of the experience; listed on Tabelog's Top 100 tonkatsu restaurants in Japan.

results.name: Edomae Sushi at Tsukiji Outer Market
results.why_it_is_special: Tokyo is the birthplace of Edomae (Edo-style) sushi, and Tsukiji Outer Market remains the city's most iconic spot for early-morning sushi using the freshest seasonal seafood — especially tuna, squid, and uni.

results.name: Yakitori under the tracks at Yurakucho
results.why_it_is_special: The smoky yakitori stalls tucked beneath the JR railway tracks near Yurakucho Station are a quintessential after-work Tokyo experience. Salarymen have gathered here for decades to eat charcoal-grilled chicken skewers with tare sauce and cold beer.

results.name: Spring Tonkatsu at Maisen
results.why_it_is_special: Maisen changes its cabbage variety seasonally; the spring-cabbage tonkatsu elevates an everyday dish into something special. A local favourite that reflects Tokyo's deep connection between food and seasonality.

results.name: Ramen at Konjiki Hototogisu
results.why_it_is_special: A Michelin-recognised ramen shop known for its clam shio (salt-based) broth — a refined, umami-rich style that represents the innovative end of Tokyo's 10,000-shop ramen scene.

results.name: Izakaya hopping in Koenji / Shimokitazawa
results.why_it_is_special: These neighbourhoods are where locals actually eat and drink — independent restaurants, tiny izakayas, and teishoku (set-meal) shops far from the tourist trail. Reliably good, affordable, and authentically Tokyo.

results.name: Taiyaki & Dango street snacks
results.why_it_is_special: Fish-shaped taiyaki (filled with red bean, custard, or sweet potato) and dango (rice-flour dumplings with sweet soy glaze) are classic Tokyo street sweets best enjoyed while strolling through Asakusa's temple district or Tsukiji's outer stalls.

results.name: Depachika seasonal bento
results.why_it_is_special: Department-store basement food halls ("depachika") are a uniquely Japanese institution. They offer exquisite seasonal bento, wagashi, and prepared foods that rotate with the calendar — a window into how Tokyoites actually eat day-to-day.
